paper_title: Tests of the Gravitational Inverse-Square Law
suggested_experiment_name: ISL tests envelope (Stanford, Lamoreaux, Moscow, Colorado, Eot-Wash, Irvine)
coupling_convention: |alpha| as plotted: dimensionless Yukawa strength relative to Newtonian gravity, alpha in V(r) = -(G m1 m2 / r)[1 + alpha exp(-r/lambda)]; x converted from Yukawa range lambda via m[eV] = 1.240e-6 / lambda[m]
notes: This is a 2003 Annual Review article (Adelberger, Heckel & Nelson) reviewing tests of the gravitational inverse-square law. It compiles existing 95%-CL constraints on Yukawa-type ISL violations parameterized as alpha (strength relative to gravity) vs lambda (range), which corresponds to ScalarNucleon-type fifth-force constraints. However, it presents no NEW experimental limit of its own; all exclusion curves (Eot-Wash, Colorado, Stanford microcantilever, Casimir, LLR/Keplerian) are from cited primary references and are shown only in figures (Figs 4, 5, 9) with no extractable numerical data in the text. A few discrete statements exist (e.g., alpha >= 16/3 excluded for lambda > 130 um; R* <= 155 um for alpha = 8/3), but these are alpha-lambda values, not coupling-vs-mass points in the requested convention. No new limit data extracted. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Traced Figure 5 (page 77) of Adelberger, Heckel & Nelson, 'Tests of the Gravitational Inverse-Square Law': 95%-CL upper limits on ISL-violating Yukawa strength |alpha| vs range lambda (1 um < lambda < 1 cm; x-axis 1e-6 to 1e-2 m, y-axis 1e-4 to 1e10 per given calibration). The excluded (yellow) region lies above the envelope formed by Stanford, Lamoreaux, Moscow, Colorado, Eot-Wash and Irvine curves. Lambda was converted to mass with m[eV]=1.240e-6/lambda[m] as instructed; note mass increases as lambda decreases, so small masses correspond to the long-range (Irvine/Eot-Wash) end. Boundary values digitized from plot; uncertainties ~factor 1.5-2 in alpha in the steep regions.
